entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of Philippi, fought on October 3, 42 BCE, was a pivotal event in the Roman Civil War, marking a decisive victory for the Second Triumvirate, led by Mark Antony, against Brutus and Cassius, two prominent leaders of the Optimates.

This brutal and bloody confrontation took place in Philippi, a strategic city in northeastern Greece, and witnessed the deaths of many prominent figures, including Brutus and Cassius.

The aftermath of the battle saw the Second Triumvirate consolidate its power, paving the way for the rise of the Julio-Claudian dynasty, which would shape the course of Roman history for centuries to come.

In a poignant twist of fate, the Battle of Philippi marked the end of an era, as the last remnants of the Roman Republic succumbed to the forces of Antony and Octavian, who would soon become Augustus, the first emperor of Rome.
